questions.question: What does COTS integration/reuse refer to in the context of system development?

options.A: Creating custom components from scratch for each project
options.B: Incorporating off‑the‑shelf (commercial) components together with newly developed ones
options.C: Outsourcing all development tasks to external vendors
options.D: Removing all reusable components from the system architecture

questions.explanation:
COTS integration/reuse means that off‑the‑shelf (commercial) components are combined with newly developed components, as described on [Page 49].

---

questions.question: According to the architecture overview, why should architectural components that are reused be highlighted?

options.A: To hide them from the testing team
options.B: To ensure they are removed during final deployment
options.C: To make their presence and impact on the system clear to stakeholders
options.D: To indicate they must be rewritten later

questions.explanation:
The text states that reused architectural components should be highlighted so their role in the system is evident, as noted on [Page 28].

---

questions.question: During system testing, what is the primary activity involving reusable components and off‑the‑shelf systems?

options.A: Isolating them to avoid any interaction with new code
options.B: Integrating them with newly developed components before testing the complete system
options.C: Deleting them after each test run
options.D: Replacing them with mock objects for verification

questions.explanation:
Page 49 explains that reusable components and off‑the‑shelf systems are integrated with newly developed components before the whole system is tested.

---

questions.question: Which type of interface is described as one where a component encapsulates procedures that other components can call, and is used by objects and reusable components?
questions.explanation:
Page 47 defines procedural interfaces as the form used by objects and reusable components.

---

questions.question: How can partition testing support the verification of COTS reusable components?

options.A: By testing only the custom code and ignoring COTS parts
options.B: By designing test cases that cover both whole systems and individual components, including COTS parts
options.C: By replacing COTS components with stubs before testing
options.D: By limiting tests to performance metrics only

questions.explanation:
Page 44 states that partition testing can be used to design test cases for both systems and components, which includes COTS reusable parts.

---

questions.question: In the system requirements specification, where is it appropriate to define interfaces to other (including COTS) systems?

options.A: Only in the user requirements section
options.B: In the non‑functional requirements portion of the specification
options.C: In the architectural component list, without any textual description
options.D: In the implementation code comments only

questions.explanation:
The context on Page 28 notes that interfaces to other systems, such as COTS, may be defined in the non‑functional requirements.

---

questions.question: What is a key advantage of using procedural interfaces for reusable components?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any documentation
options.B: They allow other components to invoke well‑defined operations without needing to know internal details
options.C: They guarantee that the component will never change
options.D: They automatically generate user interface screens

questions.explanation:
Procedural interfaces encapsulate procedures that can be called by other components, providing abstraction, as described on Page 47.

---

questions.question: When planning the high‑level system architecture, what should be done with components that are identified for reuse?

options.A: They should be marked for future removal
options.B: They should be highlighted to indicate their reuse status
options.C: They should be merged with custom code to hide their origin
options.D: They should be ignored during risk analysis

questions.explanation:
The architecture overview on Page 28 advises that reused components be highlighted.

---

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the relationship between system testing and COTS reuse?

options.A: COTS components are tested only once, before integration
options.B: System testing validates the interaction between COTS components and newly developed parts together
options.C: COTS components are exempt from any testing because they are commercial products
options.D: System testing focuses solely on performance, not on integration of COTS parts

questions.explanation:
Page 49 explains that during system testing, both reusable (including COTS) and newly developed components are integrated and tested as a complete system.

---

questions.question: Why is it recommended to use natural language, simple tables, and intuitive diagrams when documenting requirements that may involve COTS components?

options.A: Because COTS vendors only accept formal mathematical specifications
options.B: To ensure that all stakeholders, including those unfamiliar with software jargon, can understand the requirements and interfaces
options.C: To comply with a mandatory industry standard that forbids technical language
options.D: To make the document longer and more detailed

questions.explanation: Page 20 advises using natural language and simple notations so that non‑technical stakeholders can comprehend requirements, which is important when describing interfaces to COTS components.
